author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Compare plugged-in and battery PS2 performance safely
summary: Separate charging heat from power-source policy by comparing matched routes, battery ranges, cable states, and temperature checkpoints without cycling a hot phone repeatedly or treating a brief turbo result as sustained performance.
heroAlt: Performance mode prompt used to illustrate that power-source policies can change emulator timing

blocks.text: Treat cable power and charging heat as separate variables

Connecting a charger can enable a vendor performance policy, create additional heat, or do both. A ten-minute plugged-in run may begin faster and finish slower than battery because charging heat consumes thermal headroom. Compare interval curves from the same route and record whether the battery is actively charging, merely powered, or already full. Use an ordinary supported charger and stop on warnings.
Never cover the device, bypass charging protections, use a damaged cable, or force repeated hot charge cycles for a benchmark. Stop if Android reports a temperature or charging fault.

items: A fixed sustained route with checkpoints at two-minute intervals.
A supported charger, intact cable, and dry ventilated test area.
A middle battery range that can support the unplugged pass.
Matched starting temperature, case, brightness, and Android power mode.
The same renderer, driver, profile, capture method, and background state.

blocks.text: Compare curves rather than peak numbers

items: 1. Begin unplugged at the documented battery and thermal baseline.
2. Run the route and record emulation speed, frame time, battery level, and thermal status at every checkpoint.
3. Let the device cool naturally back to baseline.
4. Connect the supported charger and verify whether Android reports active charging.
5. Repeat the route from the same save without touching emulator settings.
6. Mark any early improvement and any later decline separately.
7. If charging heat dominates, perform an optional short powered test only after a full cool-down and within manufacturer guidance.
8. Choose everyday settings from the slower sustained condition, not the best opening minute.

blocks.text: Interval records reveal whether cable connection changes policy immediately or heat accumulates gradually. An immediate stable gain suggests a source-dependent performance rule; a delayed loss that follows rising thermal status suggests charging heat. Both can exist, so the result should describe the curve instead of a single winner.
The comparison is valid when the route and starting state match and the device remains within normal operating behavior.

items: Both passes begin at comparable temperature and charge range.
Charging state and charger type are recorded explicitly.
No emulator or display setting changes between passes.
Checkpoint timing shows when the curves diverge.
A repeated run confirms the same qualitative pattern.
Charging pauses due to temperature: stop and discard the pass.
The battery reaches an automatic power threshold in one run: normalize the range.
A system update or game mode changes between tests: begin a new comparison.
Only a menu is measured: repeat with sustained gameplay.

blocks.text: Return to ordinary charging and play habits

Disconnect the diagnostic setup, let the phone cool before continued charging, restore the normal case and brightness, and remove monitoring overlays. Do not leave a charger-specific aggressive profile enabled when its sustained advantage was not proven.
Full charge is not necessarily a neutral plugged state

Some devices continue drawing power, trickle-charge, or change thermal policy near full capacity. Document the exact state shown by Android and avoid generalizing from a single charger, cable, or battery-health condition.
